prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: spectacular newspaper feature cover and reusable team scene. Generate ONE new cinematic very wide 2:1 landscape illustration, 2400x1200 or larger if possible. This is a freshly staged, exuberant new episode in the ARC Daily Digest SCORING HALL: a BREAKDANCE CYPHER, The Last Dance taking the floor. The four dancers are the STARS, all clearly visible large in the central foreground, with the other contenders standing around watching in delight. The Last Dance characters are compact small ADULTS, about three quarters the height of the ordinary adult spectators; this is an affectionate editorial size convention, not a medical statement or children. Input 1 is the AUTHORITATIVE four-person costume/character sheet. Preserve each identity and distinctive outfit exactly: Lukas, swept brown hair, clean-shaven blue-eyed cartoon face, navy hoodie and blue-dominant ARC-grid suit; Florian, black baseball cap, black sunglasses and dark stubble, orange/red-dominant ARC-grid bomber over black shirt; Mykyta, tousled light-brown hair and full reddish-brown beard, cyan/green ARC-grid tracksuit; fourth dancer an entirely fictional anonymous opaque black helmet with four yellow square lights and purple/yellow ARC-grid suit. The helmet is NOT a verified likeness of Günter Klambauer or anyone else. No goose or other bird substitute for that dancer.

Floor: a spectacular luminous square ARC puzzle grid dance floor set into polished dark stone. Saturated blue, red, green, yellow, magenta, cyan, orange, white, black squares form asymmetric recognizably ARC puzzle shapes, not a generic rainbow checkerboard. Crisp black grid lines, reflections of the dancers, bright disco spotlights, warm gold lanterns. The four dance wildly in FOUR distinct energetic breakdance poses with physical contact to floor and readable faces: Lukas at center-front in a magnificent one-hand side freeze, torso turned so face is visible, bent legs flying diagonally; Florian just left performs a deep six-step sweep with cap and sunglasses in place, one hand braced and one leg extended; bearded Mykyta on the right in a low airborne kick/freeze, head and beard unobscured; helmeted purple/yellow dancer farther center-back in an ecstatic one-hand handstand with legs split. Use convincing anatomy, exactly two arms and two legs per dancer, no fused hands or borrowed limbs. Leave enough space between each dancer to see their silhouette and costume. Their crazy ARC suits should explode with color against the hall. All four dancers equal visual importance, camera low enough for drama but high enough to read the whole dance floor.

Input 2 supplies only the monumental scoring hall architecture, painterly polished 3D-comic world, and established audience identities. New camera, new blocking, no reproduction of its giant-cat arrival composition. Bronze gothic-industrial vaults, tall open arches showing moonlit snowy mountains and illuminated distant castle. A joyful sporting spectacle, dramatic blue/amber rim light, glittering tiny square confetti, energetic body language. The audience is a loose semicircle behind and on both sides, looking DOWN AND IN toward the small dancers. Keep foreground and floor unobstructed. The giant cream-white blue-eyed xz cat is now a delighted SPECTATOR at the far right rear, sitting quietly with its cyber vest and fluffy plume tail visible; its head does not dominate the cover and is smaller in the image than the dance group. Chen's EXACT TWO bunnies, gray lop with both ears DOWN and brown-and-white upright-eared bunny with broad white face blaze, watch from front-left edge off the dance floor. Tufa: tall clean-shaven brown-haired Dries with GREEN square eyepiece and black tech suit, plus FIVE friendly little black fluffy spiders with big white eyes, all watching and enjoying the show at left rear. NVIDIA pair Jean-Francois Puget bearded with dark glasses and Ivan clean-shaven short brown hair cyan collar, both with green-accent cyber engineer gear, stand behind the dance floor enjoying it. No corporate logos.

Input 3 supplies the FULL seven-person Team Turducken audience and TWO Yorkies. Keep all seven together along the back of the dance circle, easy to spot: muscular tattooed bearded Mark in black cyber gear and gold chain; Son separate Asian cyber-engineer with broad BLUE VISOR and black GPU headgear; Keith little yellow mascot black cap; DZ blonde chibi holding pink bunny; NT orange kitten in banana suit with comic tears; Choryu rectangular grayscale MRI display head; Herminator silver/cobalt knight with BLUE PLUME. Exactly two small Yorkies beside Mark at the edge. They are laughing, cheering, pointing at the dance moves, standing or sitting, none duplicated. A modest mechanical turkey parked behind them ties the world together without blocking the party. Audience detail secondary to the four brilliantly dressed dancers, all four dancers' full bodies and limbs must remain readable.

High back wall contains a huge decorative dark leaderboard with luminous abstract colored grid motifs ONLY, no ranks or scores or names. This is an evergreen team feature, not a depiction of a new result. Integrated elegant dark bottom newspaper masthead strip with EXACT legible gold/ivory text 'THE ARC DAILY DIGEST' at left, 'THE LAST DANCE TAKES THE FLOOR' center, '29 OCTOBER 2026' at right and very small 'AI editorial illustration'. No other text, speech bubbles, numerical scores, logos or watermarks. Luxurious tactile fur and cloth, polished brass, colorful floor bounce light, enormously fun kinetic energy. Match the warm, richly detailed and affectionate cinematic fantasy of the references. All characters are respectful stylized editorial avatars. Do not depict a real event or their actual computing hardware.

references.role: The four Last Dance editorial dancers: three verified likenesses and a deliberately fictional masked fourth account
Established hall and spectator character references, not its historical scoreboard
Seven-person Turducken spectator crew and two Yorkies

review: Inspected four distinct adult breakdancers in colorful ARC-grid streetwear on a luminous square floor: cap-and-sunglasses Florian left, swept-hair Lukas front center, bearded Mykyta right, fictional opaque-helmet fourth account behind. Full distinct limbs and readable costumes. Scoring-hall audience includes seven Turducken characters, two Yorkies, two Chen rabbits, Dries and friendly spiders, Puget/Ivan and xz cat. Masthead and date legible; no scores or claim of a real dance event. Fourth account is explicitly a fictional stand-in, not a goose or verified human likeness.
